title: Amos Chapter 5 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Amos chapter 5 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Amos Chapter 5 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Amos Chapter 5.

questions.question: What type of message is Amos taking up against the house of Israel?
questions.explanation: Amos 5:1 states that the word taken up against the house of Israel is a lamentation.

questions.question: According to Amos, what has happened to the virgin of Israel?
options: She is fallen and shall no more rise
She is protected by the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: She is fallen and shall no more rise
questions.explanation: Amos 5:2 says the virgin of Israel is fallen and shall no more rise, being forsaken upon her land.

questions.question: What will happen to a city that went out by a thousand, according to the LORD GOD?
questions.explanation: Amos 5:3 says the city that went out by a thousand shall leave an hundred, showing a great reduction.

questions.question: What does the LORD command the house of Israel to do so that they may live?
questions.explanation: Amos 5:4 clearly states the LORD's command to seek Him so that they may live.

questions.question: Which places does the LORD instruct the people NOT to seek or enter?
questions.explanation: Amos 5:5 commands not to seek Bethel, enter Gilgal, or pass to Beersheba.

questions.question: What will happen to Gilgal and Bethel according to Amos?
options: Gilgal shall go into captivity and Bethel shall come to nought
They will be places of worship renewed
questions.correctAnswer: Gilgal shall go into captivity and Bethel shall come to nought
questions.explanation: Amos 5:5 states that Gilgal shall surely go into captivity and Bethel shall come to nought.

questions.question: What warning is given if the people do not seek the LORD?
options: He will break out like fire in the house of Joseph and devour it
They will have peace and prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: He will break out like fire in the house of Joseph and devour it
questions.explanation: Amos 5:6 warns that if they do not seek the LORD, He will break out like fire and devour the house of Joseph.

questions.question: What do the people turn judgment into, as mentioned in Amos 5?
questions.explanation: Amos 5:7 mentions that the people turn judgment into wormwood and leave off righteousness.

questions.question: Who does Amos say made the seven stars and Orion?
questions.explanation: Amos 5:8 identifies the LORD as the maker of the seven stars and Orion.

questions.question: According to Amos, what does the LORD do with the waters of the sea?
options: Pours them out upon the face of the earth
questions.correctAnswer: Pours them out upon the face of the earth
questions.explanation: Amos 5:8 states the LORD calls for the waters of the sea and pours them out upon the face of the earth.

questions.question: Who strengthens the spoiled against the strong, according to Amos?
questions.explanation: Amos 5:9 says the LORD strengthens the spoiled against the strong.

questions.question: True or False: Amos 5:10 states that the people love him that rebuketh in the gate.
questions.explanation: Amos 5:10 says that they hate him that rebuketh in the gate and abhor him that speaketh uprightly, so the statement is false.

questions.question: Which command comes first in Amos 5:4-6?
options: Seek ye me, and ye shall live
Seek the LORD, and ye shall live
questions.correctAnswer: Seek ye me, and ye shall live
questions.explanation: Amos 5:4 is the earliest command in this sequence, instructing to seek the LORD for life before the prohibitions in verses 5 and 6.

questions.question: True or False: Amos 5:7 condemns those who leave off righteousness in the earth.
questions.explanation: Amos 5:7 rebukes those who turn judgment to wormwood and leave off righteousness, confirming the truth of the statement.

questions.question: True or False: Amos 5:6 encourages seeking the LORD so He may bless the vineyards of Israel.
questions.explanation: Amos 5:6 encourages seeking the LORD to live and avoid destruction, not specifically to bless vineyards; thus, the statement is false.

medium.title: Amos Chapter 5 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Amos Chapter 5 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Amos 5:10, how do the people respond to those who rebuke and speak uprightly in the gate?
options: They honor and listen to them
questions.explanation: Amos 5:10 states that the people hate him that rebuketh in the gate and abhor him that speaketh uprightly, showing their rejection of righteous correction.

questions.question: What consequence does Amos 5:11 describe for those who oppress the poor and build houses of hewn stone?
options: They will not dwell in their houses or drink wine from their vineyards
They will be blessed with abundance
They will become rulers over others
They will receive honor in the city
questions.correctAnswer: They will not dwell in their houses or drink wine from their vineyards
questions.explanation: Amos 5:11 explains that despite building fine houses and planting vineyards, those who oppress the poor will not enjoy these blessings, indicating divine judgment on their injustice.

questions.question: Based on Amos 5:12, which of the following sins are the people guilty of?
options: Afflicting the just, taking bribes, and turning aside the poor from their right
Stealing from the temple and worshiping idols
Ignoring the poor and fasting without sincerity
questions.correctAnswer: Afflicting the just, taking bribes, and turning aside the poor from their right
questions.explanation: Amos 5:12 clearly lists manifold transgressions including afflicting the just, accepting bribes, and denying the poor justice, revealing systemic corruption.

questions.question: What does Amos 5:13 suggest the prudent will do during the evil time described?
questions.explanation: Amos 5:13 says the prudent will keep silence because it is an evil time, indicating that wise people may avoid speaking out when conditions are perilous.

questions.question: What will happen if the people seek good and not evil, according to Amos 5:14?
options: They shall live and the LORD God of hosts shall be with them
They will be ignored by God
questions.correctAnswer: They shall live and the LORD God of hosts shall be with them
questions.explanation: Amos 5:14 promises life and God's presence to those who seek good and not evil, highlighting the importance of pursuing righteousness for survival and divine favor.

questions.question: What attitude does Amos 5:15 instruct believers to adopt towards evil and good?
options: Hate evil, love good, and establish judgment in the gate
Accept both evil and good equally
questions.correctAnswer: Hate evil, love good, and establish judgment in the gate
questions.explanation: Amos 5:15 calls for hatred of evil, love for good, and the establishment of just judgment, emphasizing active moral discernment and justice in society.

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'wailing' mentioned in Amos 5:16?
options: It signifies mourning and lamentation throughout the streets and highways
It celebrates a festival of joy
It signals a victory over enemies
It indicates a time of peace and prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies mourning and lamentation throughout the streets and highways
questions.explanation: Amos 5:16 describes wailing as a form of mourning in all streets and highways, indicating widespread grief as a consequence of God’s judgment.

questions.question: According to Amos 5:17, where will the wailing take place and why?
options: In all vineyards, because the LORD will pass through
Only in the temple, because worshippers are unfaithful
In the marketplaces, because of famine
In the fields, because of drought
questions.correctAnswer: In all vineyards, because the LORD will pass through
questions.explanation: Amos 5:17 states that wailing will occur in all vineyards because the LORD will pass through, symbolizing God’s judgment touching places of prosperity.

questions.question: What warning is given in Amos 5:18 regarding those who desire the day of the LORD?
options: It will bring darkness and not light
It will bring joy and celebration
questions.correctAnswer: It will bring darkness and not light
questions.explanation: Amos 5:18 warns that the day of the LORD will be darkness, not light, for those desiring it, indicating that God’s judgment will be severe rather than favorable.

questions.question: How does Amos 5:19 describe the experience of those expecting the day of the LORD?
options: Like fleeing from a lion only to meet a bear, or being bitten by a serpent at home
Like a victorious warrior returning home
Like a shepherd caring for his sheep
questions.correctAnswer: Like fleeing from a lion only to meet a bear, or being bitten by a serpent at home
questions.explanation: Amos 5:19 uses vivid imagery of danger and unexpected harm to illustrate that those expecting the day of the LORD will face successive calamities instead of relief.

questions.question: True or False: According to Amos 5:20, the day of the LORD will be filled with brightness and light.
questions.explanation: Amos 5:20 explicitly states the day of the LORD will be darkness, not light, very dark with no brightness, refuting the idea of it being filled with light.

questions.question: True or False: Amos 5:21 indicates God is pleased with the people's feast days and solemn assemblies.
questions.explanation: Amos 5:21 reveals God's hatred and despising of their feast days and solemn assemblies, showing that mere ritual without righteousness is unacceptable.

questions.question: True or False: In Amos 5:22, God says He will accept burnt offerings and peace offerings from the people despite their sins.
questions.explanation: Amos 5:22 states God will not accept their burnt offerings, meat offerings, or peace offerings, emphasizing that offerings alone cannot substitute for justice and righteousness.

questions.question: What does Amos 5:23 say God wants removed from the people's worship?
options: The noise of their songs and the melody of their viols
questions.correctAnswer: The noise of their songs and the melody of their viols
questions.explanation: Amos 5:23 expresses God's rejection of the noise of their songs and melodies in worship because they are empty without justice and righteousness.

questions.question: According to Amos 5:24, what should flow like waters and a mighty stream?
questions.explanation: Amos 5:24 calls for judgment to run down as waters and righteousness as a mighty stream, emphasizing the importance of justice and moral integrity.

hard.title: Amos Chapter 5 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Amos Chapter 5.

questions.question: According to Amos 5:19, what analogy is used to describe the inescapable judgment upon Israel?
options: A man fleeing from a lion but meeting a bear
A man walking into a lion's den unarmed
A serpent biting a man who fled from a bear
A man climbing a tree to escape a lion
questions.correctAnswer: A man fleeing from a lion but meeting a bear
questions.explanation: Amos 5:19 uses the analogy of a man fleeing from a lion only to meet a bear, illustrating unavoidable calamity.

questions.question: What does Amos 5:20 say about 'the day of the LORD'?
options: It will be a day of great light and joy
It will be darkness and not light
It will be a day of peace and prosperity
It will be a day of celebration and feasting
questions.correctAnswer: It will be darkness and not light
questions.explanation: Amos 5:20 clearly states the day of the LORD will be darkness and not light, emphasizing judgment rather than blessing.

questions.question: How does the LORD describe Israel's feast days in Amos 5:21?
questions.explanation: Amos 5:21 states God hates and despises Israel's feast days and will not accept their assemblies.

questions.question: What is the LORD's response to burnt offerings and peace offerings in Amos 5:22?
options: He demands sacrifices from other nations
questions.explanation: Amos 5:22 declares that despite offerings, God will not accept them because Israel's actions contradict true worship.

questions.question: What does Amos 5:23 say about the music and songs of Israel?
options: Their songs are pleasing to the LORD
God refuses to hear their noise and melody
Their viols bring joy to the congregation
questions.correctAnswer: God refuses to hear their noise and melody
questions.explanation: Amos 5:23 emphasizes God rejecting the noise of their songs and melodies because of their hypocrisy.

questions.question: What is the righteous standard that Amos 5:24 calls for?
options: Judgment flowing like waters and righteousness like a mighty stream
Peace and prosperity for all nations
Sacrifices and offerings accepted by God
Songs and celebrations in the temple
questions.correctAnswer: Judgment flowing like waters and righteousness like a mighty stream
questions.explanation: Amos 5:24 poetically calls for justice and righteousness to prevail continuously and powerfully.

questions.question: In Amos 5:25, what question does the LORD ask Israel regarding sacrifices?
options: Have you worshipped other gods in secret?
Have you offered sacrifices and offerings in the wilderness forty years?
Have you kept the Sabbath holy?
Have you built new altars for the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Have you offered sacrifices and offerings in the wilderness forty years?
questions.explanation: Amos 5:25 recalls Israel’s historical offerings in the wilderness, questioning their present faithfulness.

questions.question: Which false gods are mentioned in Amos 5:26 as being carried by Israel?
questions.explanation: Amos 5:26 specifically names Moloch and Chiun as idols Israel bore, indicating idolatry despite God's commands.

questions.question: What consequence does the LORD declare in Amos 5:27 for Israel's idolatry?
options: Peace and restoration in their land
questions.explanation: Amos 5:27 pronounces exile beyond Damascus as punishment for Israel’s idolatry and rebellion.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage echoes the theme of rejecting mere ritual without righteousness as Amos 5:21-24 does?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 1:11-17 similarly condemns empty sacrifices without justice and righteousness, paralleling Amos 5:21-24.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes Amos 5:24's call for justice and righteousness?
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:23 highlights justice, mercy, and faithfulness, echoing Amos 5:24’s demand for justice and righteousness.

questions.question: What Hebrew word meaning 'justice' or 'judgment' is central to Amos 5:24 and often used throughout the book of Amos?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Mishpat' meaning 'justice' or 'judgment' is key to Amos 5:24’s call for judgment to flow like waters.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Amos 5:19 to convey the inevitability of judgment?
questions.explanation: Amos 5:19 uses a simile comparing fleeing from a lion but meeting a bear to illustrate inescapable judgment.

questions.question: True or False: Amos 5:22-23 declares that God will accept Israel’s burnt offerings if they are accompanied by proper music and songs.
questions.explanation: Amos 5:22-23 states God will not accept offerings nor hear the melody of songs because Israel’s worship is hypocritical.

questions.question: True or False: Amos 5:18-20 warns that the day of the LORD will be a day of darkness and judgment rather than joy and light.
questions.explanation: Amos 5:18-20 clearly warns that the day of the LORD will be darkness and not light, signaling judgment rather than blessing.

theological.title: Amos Chapter 5 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Amos Chapter 5 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Amos 5:4 urge the house of Israel to do?
questions.explanation: Amos 5:4 specifically states, 'For thus saith the LORD unto the house of Israel, Seek ye me, and ye shall live:' indicating that seeking God is essential for life.

questions.question: According to Amos 5:18, what is the nature of the day of the LORD?
questions.explanation: Amos 5:18 declares, 'Woe unto you that desire the day of the LORD! to what end is it for you? the day of the LORD is darkness, and not light.' This emphasizes the seriousness of the day.

questions.question: What does Amos 5:24 emphasize should flow like water?
questions.explanation: Amos 5:24 states, 'But let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream,' advocating for justice and righteousness in society.

questions.question: What kind of judgment does God express in Amos 5:21 regarding Israel's feasts?
questions.explanation: In Amos 5:21, God states, 'I hate, I despise your feast days,' showing His displeasure with empty rituals devoid of true worship.

questions.question: What warning does Amos 5:6 give to those who seek the Lord?
questions.explanation: Amos 5:6 emphasizes, 'Seek the LORD, and ye shall live; lest he break out like fire in the house of Joseph,' indicating that seeking God leads to life.

questions.question: What does Amos 5:12 reveal about the sins of Israel?
questions.explanation: Amos 5:12 states, 'For I know your manifold transgressions and your mighty sins,' indicating the seriousness and multitude of their sins.

questions.question: In Amos 5:10, who is hated by the people for speaking uprightly?
questions.explanation: Amos 5:10 states, 'They hate him that rebuketh in the gate, and they abhor him that speaketh uprightly,' indicating the rejection of truth-tellers.

questions.question: What does Amos 5:15 instruct the Israelites to do regarding good and evil?
questions.explanation: Amos 5:15 emphasizes, 'Seek good, and not evil, that ye may live,' urging the people to pursue righteousness.

questions.question: What metaphor does Amos 5:19 use to describe the day of the LORD?
questions.explanation: Amos 5:19 uses the metaphor, 'As if a man did flee from a lion, and a bear met him,' illustrating the inevitable danger of the day of the LORD.

questions.question: What does Amos 5:26 highlight about Israel's worship practices?
options: They bore the tabernacle of Moloch
They were pure in their offerings
questions.correctAnswer: They bore the tabernacle of Moloch
questions.explanation: Amos 5:26 states, 'But ye have borne the tabernacle of your Moloch and Chiun your images,' indicating that they incorporated idolatry into their worship.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated in Amos 5:8 regarding His creative power?
questions.explanation: Amos 5:8 highlights God's creative authority, 'Seek him that maketh the seven stars and Orion,' showcasing His power over creation.

questions.question: According to Amos 5:17, what will occur in all vineyards?
questions.explanation: Amos 5:17 states, 'And in all vineyards shall be wailing: for I will pass through thee,' indicating impending judgment.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Amos 5:3 and 5:11 convey about the fate of Israel?
questions.explanation: Amos 5:3 describes a diminishing remnant, while Amos 5:11 illustrates their loss of material wealth, indicating a fate of devastation.

questions.question: What does Amos 5:13 imply about the wise during evil times?
questions.explanation: Amos 5:13 indicates, 'Therefore the prudent shall keep silence in that time; for it is an evil time,' suggesting wisdom in restraint.

questions.question: What does Amos 5:14 promise regarding the presence of the LORD?
options: He will be with those who seek good
He will rejoice in their feasts
questions.correctAnswer: He will be with those who seek good
questions.explanation: Amos 5:14 states, 'and so the LORD, the God of hosts, shall be with you, as ye have spoken,' emphasizing God's presence with the righteous.
